- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is speaking at a campaign stop
in Swing State, Arizona right now,
and a Republican-leaning congressional district
in Montana later today.
The visits come as Trump works to bolster his party
ahead of the midterms that will determine control
of Congress.
Trump's stops so far this month have taken him
into traditionally solid Republican territory
in Alabama, Nebraska, Ohio, Tennessee, and Texas
as he weathers low approval ratings, rising costs,
and the Iran war.
Family members of Minnesota Democratic Congresswoman
Ilhan Omar are being subpoenaed as part

- Immigration agents searched Omar's DC home one day.
The Justice Department said it was part
of a federal criminal investigation.
According to an official familiar with,

the probe has now expanded with subpoenas issued

that Omar investigation centers

a break with the DOJ's 60-day rule.
This norm is meant to protect elections
from politically motivated law enforcement.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
The Social Security Administration projects
a 3.6% cost of living increase on checks for older adults
and people with disabilities starting in 2027.
Some recipients say it won't offset rising prices.
The adjustment means $75 extra per month
for the nearly 72 million social security beneficiaries
and about 7.3 million supplemental
security income recipients.
A major source of fraud in the SNAP Federal Food Aid Program
is to do with its outdated security features,
NPR's Juliana Kim reports hundreds of millions of dollars
have been stolen from SNAP recipients
as a result in Congress is now considering upgrading the tech.
In most states, food assistance cards rely on swipe pay
with magnetic stripes, leaving them extremely vulnerable
to a type of fraud known as card skimming.
Democratic Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon
has been pushing for cards to have microchips,
which is the standard for most debit and credit cards today.
We've been hearing the Republicans talk
about rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in hunger programs.
My bill gives you a way to do it
without taking food away from hungry children.
The Senate version of the Farm Bill
includes a provision to roll out trips,
but the House version does not,
meaning it's unclear if the measure will make the final cut.
Juliana Kim, NPR News.
U.S. inflation accelerated last month
as gas, clothes, and airfares got more expensive.
It's evidence that rising prices remain an economic challenge
just a few weeks before the midterm elections.
The Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% in September,
compared with a year ago.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Justice Department is threatening California
with possible legal action over what it says
are non-citizens who received mail ballots
for next month's midterm elections.
A letter sent to the Secretary of State
gives California 48 hours to determine
whether any non-citizens are listed.
-Monarch butterflies are migrating south,
and this fall, scientists have a new way
to see where they go on their long journey.
Vermont Public's Abigail Giles reports
they're rigging them with tiny backpacks
with solar-powered trackers.
-That's the sound of a monarch butterfly rustling its legs.
Biologist Desiree Norango is holding it very gently
by the abdomen in her Vermont lab.
-To hold a butterfly, this part right here,
this part of the vein, is the strongest part,
so you can hold that safely.
-Next, Norango attaches a tiny transmitter
to the butterfly's abdomen using non-toxic eyelash glue
before releasing it outside to start its migration.
The transmitter uses Bluetooth to ping off of cell phones
and create a map of the butterfly's travels.
Norango is part of an international effort
to track the insects this way.
The hope is to learn more about where they face threats
to better protect them.
For NPR News, I'm Abigail Giles in White River Junction, Vermont.
Americans have a new sunscreen option
for the first time in over 25 years.
The FDA approved the chemical ingredient BEMT back in June.
It's now available in products from several brands.
The ingredient's already popular in Europe
and is supposed to offer broad protection
without the cosmetic downsides of older ingredients.
It also has minimal skin absorption,
reducing safety concerns unlike some older chemicals.
BEMT is stable in sunlight.

topics.text: Trump campaigns in Arizona and Montana ahead of midterms amid low approval and Iran war
Immigration agents searched Rep. Ilhan Omar's DC home; family members subpoenaed in federal probe
Social Security announces 3.6% cost-of-living increase for 2027, adding $75 monthly per beneficiary
Sen. Ron Wyden pushes microchip upgrade for SNAP cards to curb skimming fraud
U.S. inflation accelerates in September, with gas, clothing, and airfares rising 3.7%
Justice Department threatens California with legal action over non-citizens receiving mail ballots
Scientists fit monarch butterflies with solar-powered Bluetooth trackers to map migration in Vermont
FDA approves BEMT sunscreen ingredient, offering first new US option in over 25 years
